- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.30) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% relative to model output.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.30), model underestimates prices; increase forecast by 5–10% to compensate for bearish bias.
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the first 5–7 days of the 30-day horizon; apply a 2–5% upward bias to early forecast points.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a 5–10% downward correction to subsequent forecasts.
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive forecast points are below true outcome, adjust next forecast upward by 2–5% to align with recent trend.
- Sentiment volatility (rapid swings) correlates with forecast error; when sentiment shifts sharply, reduce forecast confidence and apply a 3–5% smoothing filter to avoid overreaction.
